title: Ticker ANT locks in Nasdaq: Anthropic gets listing approval, offering price $70 to $78
excerpt: SEC registration filings made public yesterday (November 17) show that Anthropic's Class A common stock has been approved to list on the Nasdaq Global Selec
content_html:
SEC registration filings made public yesterday (November 17) show that Anthropic's Class A common stock has been approved to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market—the highest-tier “premier large-cap” segment among Nasdaq's three tiers—under the ticker symbol "ANT", with the offering price range unchanged at $70 to $78 per share (about RMB 467.5 to 521). The deal, which is vying to become the largest IPO in history, has taken another step forward.

825 Million Shares Plus a $26 Billion Private Placement: Raising on Two Fronts at OnceThe filing discloses that the company plans to publicly offer 825 million Class A common shares, of which the company is offering about 801.4 million shares and existing shareholders are selling about 23.65 million shares; at the midpoint of $74, the public offering would be about $61.1 billion, and underwriters also hold an over-allotment option for up to 123.75 million shares. In addition, there is a concurrent $26 billion private placement, with Google, Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC all participating. Combined, net proceeds are expected to be about $84.6 billion, and if the over-allotment option is fully exercised, that would climb to about $93.7 billion.

Demand remains fierce: subscription demand has reached nearly seven times the shares being offered, and because existing investors are being prioritized, some new buyers may receive smaller allocations than expected. The shareholding picture is also worth noting—after the IPO, Amazon is expected to hold about 14.7% of the outstanding shares and Google about 13.7%; if Amazon's convertible notes are fully converted, its stake could reach as high as 23.8%. Also, based on the midpoint estimate, stock-based compensation-related expenses total about $6.5 billion, so the pre-IPO bill is not cheap either.
